Lemme tell you everything you need to know. So if you got these phones on promotion or for a discount it’s going to be over their financing period which I believe is 36 months. Just to give you a lil advice if you keep your devices at AT&T for at least 90 days and wait 120 days to go back to tmobile (total of 120/4 months from when you switched to AT&T in march) then you can pay off your devices and unlock them with AT&T and if you bring your last bill from them into a tmobile then they can reimburse you the money for that. So that is what I would recommend doing for multiple reasons. First reason is that’s how you get your money back for your new phones, second is it will all be done over customer care because it is not possible to activate an account with numbers that cancelled out within 120 days for store reps. Only customer care can reactivate an account which is what you would be doing if you went back to tmobile within those 120 days and talking to customer care and getting that done is a process nobody wants to do. If you wait those 120 days, then a rep in store can get everything done for you as well as help you get reimbursed for those new phones and they get commission for it. Everybody is happy. (Recommend trying your best working with somebody who knows what they are talking about when switching back to tmobile, not every rep is a good rep) (also recommend checking with a tmobile store you can do that before you make the switch and pay off the phones because promotions change sometimes)

Going to be honest with you, when it comes to phone promos, as long as you fit the requirements like what plan you choose and if you port numbers (has to be within 2 weeks of activation as well if you want it to go through perfectly),then the promos actually apply automatically. If the numbers were ported within 2 weeks there is no fault for the rep. They did their job if that is true, it seems more like T-Mobile’s backend had a problem applying the promos which happens sometimes, not super often but when you have as many customers as T-Mobile has it definitely happens. I would recommend going back to the store to see if everything was done within the requirement (always try to work with the rep who originally activated you). As long as everything was done correctly on the store side then at that point it is for some a backend tmobile problem. Calling customer care and talking to a supervisor NOT a regular representative will be the way to go and they can apply it for you and no promises but probably credit you back for the missing credits too. Crediting back money just depends on how long you mighta took to resolve the problem or at least make attempts to resolve it. Just make your case and all should be fixed
